newsitem.title: UK: IPE clarifies cancelled trades on natgas futures.
newsitem.headline: IPE clarifies cancelled trades on natgas futures.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said on Wednesday that it has given formal guidelines to members on cancellation of trades on the new natural gas futures contract.
The guidelines follow an error on the second day of the contract, when two trades using the screen-based Energy Trading System (ETS) were "bust" as bids were entered in error.

The IPE said in a statement that if a member enters a trade in error, he is requested to contact the Exchange with evidence. If the Exchange believes it is an error, it will give the firm details of the counterparty to the trade.
The firm may then contact the counterparty and seek agreement to cancel the trade. If both parties agree within 30 minutes of the deal, it will be cancelled.
If the firms do not agree, the Exchange will decide on whether to cancel.

It will only do so if it can be proved that a "manifest error" has been made. This is defined as the entry of a price one decimal point away from the intended price, for example 100p or 1p instead of 10p.

The IPE will also introduce two warning messages on to the ETS. One will warn traders who break an existing bid or offer. The other will warn traders if they enter a trade over 100 percent above or below current prices.
